## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
One test needs fixing. `test_rejects_legacy_header` does not check the version header it names, because its input has no `END` line and still uses a `REPORT v1` header. The production change in `app/report.py` is correct for the inputs this review traced. `test_rejects_unsupported_header_with_complete_report` does cover the new rejection branch, so the defect found here is Important rather than Critical.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- tests/test_report.py:10 — tests — `test_rejects_legacy_header` builds `"REPORT v1\nversion=v0"`, so `parse_report` returns `None` because the `END` line is missing (`app/report.py:3`), not because the header is checked. `fixture.rsplit("v1", 1)` replaces only the last `"v1"`, which sits in the body line `version=v1`. The header stays `REPORT v1` and no `END` line is ever added, so the test would still pass if the check at `app/report.py:5` were deleted or went back to `startswith("REPORT ")`. The comment at line 9, "changing the fixture's version to v0", describes a header change the code never makes. Recommended fix: use a complete report with a legacy header, such as `parse_report("REPORT v0\nvalue=ok\nEND") is None`, or delete the test, since `test_rejects_unsupported_header_with_complete_report` already covers that input. — The test is presented as regression protection for the version check, but it cannot catch a regression in that check, which gives maintainers false confidence.

## Suggestions
(none)

## Strengths
- `test_rejects_unsupported_header_with_complete_report` (`tests/test_report.py:15-17`) sends a complete, well-formed report with a `REPORT v0` header. That test fails under the old `startswith("REPORT ")` check and passes under the new exact match, so it really tests the change.
